planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Olympiad produces large, high-centered blooms of pure, non-fading crimson-red carrying 30 or more petals, prized by exhibitors and cut-flower growers for classic hybrid tea form and long, strong stems. The blooms carry little to no fragrance, so this rose is grown primarily for its bold color and exhibition-quality form rather than scent. Plants grow upright and vigorous with dark green, leathery foliage that sets off the intensely colored flowers. Give it full sun, good air circulation, and regular feeding through the growing season for repeated flushes of bloom.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Pascali bears pure white, high-centered double blooms with a faint ivory blush at the petal base, opening slowly from slender buds carried singly on long stems ideal for cutting. The fragrance is light and sweet rather than pronounced, and the blooms hold their form and color well in heat, unlike many white roses that bruise or pink with age. The upright bush carries large, dark green, leathery foliage and blooms reliably across a long season. It prefers full sun and consistent moisture, with routine deadheading encouraging further flushes.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Charlotte Armstrong opens from long, elegantly pointed buds into medium pink, high-centered double blooms with a darker pink reverse, borne mostly one to a stem on long cutting-length stems. It was an influential mid-twentieth-century hybrid tea, and many popular modern roses trace their ancestry back to it. The bush is vigorous and upright with good disease resistance, flowering in strong repeat flushes through the growing season. Grow in full sun with rich, well-drained soil and regular feeding to support its vigorous, continuous bloom cycle.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Miss All-American Beauty produces very large, deep rose-pink blooms packed with 50 or more petals in a full, cupped hybrid tea form, carried on long sturdy stems well suited for cutting. The flowers release a strong, old-rose-style fragrance among the most pronounced of modern hybrid teas. The plant grows into a bushy, compact shrub with glossy, leathery dark green foliage and blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through fall. It performs best in full sun with ample water and regular fertilizing to sustain its heavy, fragrant blooms.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Royal Highness carries soft, pale pink, high-centered double blooms of classic exhibition form, their satiny petals unfurling from slender buds on long straight stems. The flowers are strongly and sweetly fragrant, among the most reliably scented of the pale pink hybrid teas. Growth is upright and medium-tall, with smooth, leathery green foliage that sets off the delicate bloom color. Plant in full sun with good drainage and consistent watering, and deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering through the season.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Ingrid Bergman bears richly colored, velvety dark red blooms in a full, high-centered hybrid tea form, each flower unfurling slowly to reveal 25 to 40 densely packed petals that resist fading and weather well in heat and rain. Fragrance is light to moderate, so the appeal of this rose rests more on its clean color and weatherproof form than on scent. The bush is sturdy, upright, and disease-resistant with dark green glossy foliage, flowering in reliable flushes through the growing season. Grow in full sun with regular watering and fertilizing for continued bloom production.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Just Joey is known for its large, loosely formed double blooms of warm copper-orange shading to buff and apricot at the petal edges, with distinctive wavy, ruffled petal margins that set it apart from the smoother form of most hybrid teas. The blooms carry a pronounced, fruity-sweet fragrance and are borne singly or in small clusters on a relatively compact, bushy plant. Foliage is dark green and leathery, providing good disease resistance and a tidy garden presence. It thrives in full sun with regular watering and benefits from deadheading to prolong its long bloom season.
sources: World Federation of Rose Societies — Rose Hall of Fame

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Sutter's Gold opens from long, pointed, red-flushed buds into golden-yellow double blooms with orange overtones that fade gracefully to soft lemon as they age, giving the bush a two-toned look within a single flush. The flowers are strongly and distinctively fragrant, often described as spicy and fruity like quince, making it one of the more intensely scented classic hybrid teas. The plant grows vigorous and upright with glossy dark green foliage and notably thorny canes. Site it in full sun with well-drained soil and regular feeding to support its strong repeat bloom.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Pink Peace produces very full, deep pink double blooms with a violet-pink reverse, their densely packed 40-plus petals opening into a large, rounded hybrid tea form on a vigorous, upright bush. Its fragrance is strong and sweet, among the most pronounced of the pink hybrid teas descended from the famous 'Peace' lineage. Foliage is dark green and leathery, and the plant produces generous repeat flushes of bloom through the growing season. Grow in full sun with consistent moisture and regular fertilizing to keep the heavy flower heads coming.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container roses in early spring in full sun and well-drained, fertile soil amended with compost.

directions: Shreveport is a grandiflora rose bearing large, cupped, button-eyed blooms in a rich blend of salmon-orange and apricot, with noticeably yellow petal reverses that add depth of color as the 40-plus petals unfurl. Fragrance is mild, with a light tea-rose character rather than a strong perfume. The bush grows tall, bushy, and well-branched, producing both clustered and solitary blooms in the strong, repeated flushes typical of the grandiflora class. Give it full sun, good air circulation, and regular feeding for best disease resistance and continuous color through the season.
